messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — Elevated 502/504 error rate observed in the edge API gateway (ingress). Metrics: 502 spike from 0.3% -> 12% over 3m, p95 latency up 4x. Alert policy: ingress-gateway-5xx-rapid. Pager: oncall-rotation.

jane.sre: seeing the same in Grafana. Topology shows spike across both us-west-2 edge clusters. Rolling pools are healthy.

raj.prod: any deploys in the last 10m?

natalie.ops: no user-facing deploys. I see a burst on requests to /v1/generate from a single customer CID (acct-cust-98) — they account for ~65% of the error volume right now.

jane.sre: can we throttle or isolate that CID at the gateway? If it's overloaded backend model, we should fallback to smaller model or 429.

incident-bot: Paging note: oncall-rotation acknowledged at 4842000010.

david.gateway: I'm going to add a temporary route rule to route acct-cust-98 to a reduced-capacity backend (model-small) and enable circuit-breaker for the upstream. Applying now:
```bash
# add policy
redwoodctl route update --match "header: x-customer-id=acct-cust-98" \
  --upstream model-small --circuit-breaker 5s
```

david.gateway: done. rule applied at 4842000078.

raj.prod: after rule, 502 % dropped to ~6% in the next 30s. p95 still elevated but trending down.

jane.sre: good. Can we also enable prefix KV caching for the common prompt prefixes from that tenant? Might help token-pressure.

natalie.ops: enabling prefix caching on the route; patch submitted + rolling.

jane.sre: I'll flip on temporary request-rate limit for that CID to 10rps — we should avoid taking down other customers.

oncall-rotation: rate-limit added for acct-cust-98 at 4842000150.

jane.sre: telemetry shows overall 502 down to 2.1% now. Edge CPU on us-west-2a spiked earlier to 92% but recovered.

raj.prod: what's the customer impact? Any major customers affected?

natalie.ops: looks like ~1.7% of active calls got 5xx during peak, mostly from that tenant. A handful of downstream retries caused a queueing effect on the model hosts. No major enterprise SLAs impacted yet.

jane.sre: I recommend we keep the route isolation and rate-limit for 30m, and schedule a paused rollup to follow — want to avoid flip-flopping configs. Also open a ticket for the customer with support to coordinate slower request pacing.

sre-lead: Agreed. Also we need post-incident: identify why that tenant's traffic increased suddenly (spike or malformed requests?), and whether autoscale thresholds failed to bring additional model capacity.

david.gateway: note: during triage we observed intermittent DNS resolution errors from a subset of model nodes — possibly coincident. I've escalated to infra DNS team.

incident-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED — created incident-4842000000 in PagerDuty, ticket INC-4842.

raj.prod: timeline please: root at 4842000000, acknowledged 4842000010, route rule at 4842000078, rate-limit 4842000150, errors stabilized 4842000220, mitigations maintained until 4842000450.

natalie.ops: customer ops note: support assigned (priority outreach) and holding for customer's reply. Prepared rollback plan if they request full traffic cut.

jane.sre: moving to monitoring mode. If 5xx creeps above 3% again we escalate to full command-room.

oncall-rotation: handing off to next oncall (raj.prod) at 4842000400 — I will include all mitigations and the route change in the handoff doc.

raj.prod: taking over. I'll keep the isolation and rate-limit in place for 30m and start a postmortem doc draft. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup: 

sre-lead: good work. Reminder to capture exact logs/trace ids (see below) for the postmortem.
```
trace ids observed: 
- t-4842-1a2b3c
- t-4842-1a2b3d
logs: gateway/us-west-2a: /var/log/proxy/504-4842.log
```

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigations in place). Last updated 4842000450."
